title: [Install] Install fails with 0x80070002 when user TEMP/TMP is on RAM‑Disk
author: WHJWNAVY
summary: The issue body already contains a strong installer root-cause hypothesis and workaround, so the next useful step is a maintainer reproduction and design around elevation-safe staging rather than another generic bug-report request.

judgment.rationale: The public report spells out a narrow environment change, the failing bootstrapper stage, the error code, and a working workaround, which is enough to design around the elevated child-process staging path.
evidence: The report moves user TEMP/TMP to a RAM-disk and then reproduces a normal-user installer failure at the elevated child-process launch step.
The issue body states that the WiX Burn bootstrapper extracts the inner bundle under %TEMP%\{GUID}\.be\ and that the elevated context cannot access that file on the RAM-disk.
Restoring TEMP/TMP to a physical disk path works around the issue.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a focused installer design that stages elevation payloads in a UAC-accessible location or fails early with a precise message when the temp path cannot be shared across the elevation boundary.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked fix attempt is visible for this specific RAM-disk/UAC staging bug, and the report provides a credible installer-layer root cause.

proposed_fixes.title: Stage elevated installer payloads outside user-only RAM-disk temp paths
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The bootstrapper appears to stage the elevated child bundle under a user TEMP/TMP location that the elevated context cannot reopen when that temp path is implemented by a RAM-disk with different visibility or ACL semantics.
plan: Reproduce the installer flow with TEMP/TMP redirected to a RAM-disk and confirm the failing child-bundle path at elevation time.
Move the elevated handoff to a machine-accessible staging location or preflight the temp path and fail before elevation with a specific remediation message.
Add installer validation for redirected TEMP/TMP scenarios so the bootstrapper no longer silently reaches a file-not-found failure at elevation time.
verification: Install PowerToys with TEMP/TMP redirected to a RAM-disk and confirm the bootstrapper either succeeds or gives the new explicit preflight failure before breaking the install.
Verify the normal physical-disk TEMP/TMP path still installs successfully without regressing existing flows.

confidence.rationale: The public report is unusually specific about the failing bootstrapper boundary, but the exact staging code path still needs a maintainer-side repro because Burn/elevation behavior is partly external to the repository.

issue_context.summary: PowerToys installation fails only when TEMP/TMP points at a RAM-disk, and the report already narrows the problem to the bootstrapper’s elevated child-process handoff.
known_information: The issue includes a bootstrapper log attachment and a screenshot of the installer error.
The reporter gave concrete reproduction steps and a working workaround.
The public report already states the suspected failing extracted path under %TEMP%\{GUID}\.be\.
No assignee or linked PR is visible.
inferences: This is likely an elevation-boundary staging issue rather than a generic MSI failure.
Because the workaround is to move TEMP/TMP back to disk, the fix likely belongs in bootstrapper staging or preflight validation rather than in application payload code.
issue_context.analysis: The old automated request for a bug report ZIP is not the best next step. The report is already strong enough to justify a maintainer-side installer repro and a targeted design hypothesis.
initial_investigation: The installer repository still contains the older WinUI3Apps custom action and broader installer hardening work, but no linked issue or PR in this thread targets the RAM-disk temp/elevation scenario directly.
This issue is distinct from #49992/#49996, which focus on mixed-version WinUI3Apps copies after upgrade rather than temp-path staging before elevation.

actions.label: Approve RAM-disk installer staging design
actions.note: The report is already specific enough for installer design work; remaining uncertainty is in the exact Burn/elevation handoff implementation.

actions.label: Reproduce installer failure with RAM-disk TEMP
actions.note: Capture the exact extracted child-bundle path and elevation boundary before narrowing the bootstrapper fix.

prerequisites: Redirect user TEMP and TMP to a RAM-disk path.
Run the standard PowerToys installer as a normal user and allow it to elevate normally.
steps: Start the installer with TEMP/TMP redirected to the RAM-disk.
Proceed until the installer launches the elevated child process.
Observe whether the child bundle path under %TEMP%\{GUID}\.be\ is present and accessible to the elevated context.
Capture whether the install fails with 0x80070002 at the handoff step.
reproduce.expected_result: The installer should either complete successfully or fail early with a targeted message instead of file-not-found during elevation.
